title: Hassett is saying there's going to be a reconcilia...
content:
Hassett is saying there's going to be a reconciliation bill next year and that Congress has more fiscal room to do stimulus than people realize. 
He's basically claiming the administration's tariff revenue and deficit math is working better than expected, which opens up space in that reconciliation bill to fund things like Trump's $2,000 stimulus checks or whatever other priorities they want to push through.​
Reconciliation is Congress's special process for passing major tax and spending bills without needing 60 Senate votes, it only needs a simple majority. 
When they use reconciliation, they get a budget score that says you can increase the deficit by X amount over ten years.
If your proposals come in under that number, you've got extra room to add more stuff.
Hassett's saying the fiscal position is better than people thought, so they've got more room in that budget than originally expected. 
Basically, if tariffs are bringing in more revenue and the deficit is improving faster than anticipated, that means they can fit more spending and tax cuts into next year's reconciliation package without blowing past their limit.​
This is a signal about what's coming in 2026, and it's worth noting that Hassett is also the leading candidate to be the next Federal Reserve chairman. 
The administration is signaling they won't be fiscally constrained when building that reconciliation bill, so expect bigger stimulus and spending proposals. 
They will keep this economy running hot at least till the midterms.

HASSETT: THERE IS MORE FISCAL ROOM TO DO STIMULATIVE THINGS NOW

title: RT
content:
RT 
@MilkRoadAI
: Google's Gemini is rapidly catching up to ChatGPT in the AI chatbot competition and the data shows this is  accelerating. 
Users are spending more time in Gemini than they were before which signals they're finding genuine value in the platform. 
Also, Gemini reached roughly 100.8 million monthly downloads compared to ChatGPT's 67.8 million, showing how dramatically the momentum has shifted.​
The turning point came in September 2025 when Google released Nano Banana, a new image generation model that went viral. 
This feature drove millions of users to try Gemini and unlike a typical download spike that fades away, people are actually sticking around and using it. 
The engagement numbers show Gemini users are now spending more time per visit than ChatGPT users, which is the clearest sign that people genuinely prefer what they're experiencing.
What makes Gemini's rise particularly significant is how Google leverages its existing dominance. 
Gemini isn't just a standalone app competing on features alone. It's built into Android, Google Search, Gmail, Chrome, and Google Workspace. 
OpenAI and ChatGPT don't have this advantage because they don't control the platforms people use every day. 
This integration means millions of people encounter Gemini naturally as part of their daily digital life, not because they made a conscious choice to download a competitor.
ChatGPT still maintains a lead in daily active users with roughly 160-190 million compared to Gemini's 35 million, so it hasn't lost its position but the trajectory matters more than the current snapshot. 
Gemini's growth rate is roughly six times faster than ChatGPT's which means at current trajectories, the gap will continue narrowing.
Gemini is catching up to ChatGPT in downloads, with 100.8 million compared to 67.8 million in November, per FT: https://t.co/WhXcT7BuLa

title: Back in May 2024, Powell brushed off any talk of s...
content:
Back in May 2024, Powell brushed off any talk of stagflation and said he “didn’t see it.”
 Fast forward a year and a half: inflation is stuck above 3% and the labor market is the weakest it’s been since the pandemic. 
Now the cracks Powell dismissed are showing up everywhere and the next Fed meeting will show whether the Fed finally turns the liquidity back on before the system seizes.
